questions.title: Correct statement on sympathetic/parasympathetic transmitters
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems?

options.B: Activation of the sympathetic system causes a drop in blood pressure.

explanations.A: Correct. Acetylcholine is the cholinergic system's transmitter, and muscarinic receptors are one of the two receptor families it activates (nicotinic being the other). This receptor-transmitter pairing holds throughout the parasympathetic postganglionic synapse and the few cholinergic sympathetic exceptions.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Sympathetic activation raises, not lowers, blood pressure -- alpha-1-mediated vasoconstriction and beta-1-mediated cardiac stimulation together increase peripheral resistance and cardiac output.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Norepinephrine is the adrenergic system's transmitter and activates adrenergic (alpha/beta) receptors, not muscarinic receptors -- the two transmitter-receptor systems do not cross over.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Acetylcholine activates muscarinic and nicotinic receptors, not adrenergic receptors -- adrenergic receptors are activated by norepinephrine and epinephrine instead.

questions.learning_objective: State that acetylcholine activates muscarinic receptors and that sympathetic activation raises rather than lowers blood pressure.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Acetylcholine activates muscarinic receptors."

questions.title: Parasympathetic system is craniosacral
questions.question: Which of the following statements concerning the parasympathetic nervous system is Correct?

options.A: The parasympathetic nervous system uses epinephrine as a neurotransmitter.
options.C: The postganglionic fibers of the parasympathetic division are long, compared to those of the sympathetic system.
options.D: The preganglionic fibers of the parasympathetic division are short, compared to those of the sympathetic system.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The parasympathetic system uses acetylcholine, not epinephrine, as its transmitter at every synapse (ganglionic and postganglionic alike).
explanations.B: Correct. The parasympathetic division is described as craniosacral because its outflow leaves the CNS from cranial nerve nuclei (III, VII, IX, X) and the sacral spinal cord (S2-S4). This contrasts directly with the sympathetic system's thoracolumbar outflow (T1 to L2/L3). The two labels name opposite anatomical levels for each division, which is exactly what this quiz item tests.
explanations.C: Incorrect. It is the parasympathetic preganglionic fibres that are relatively long (travelling near to the target organ before synapsing) and the postganglionic fibres that are short -- the reverse of the sympathetic pattern, not what this option states.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Parasympathetic preganglionic fibres are relatively long, not short, since the ganglion lies near or within the target organ rather than close to the spinal cord.

questions.learning_objective: State that the parasympathetic outflow is craniosacral.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Is considered cranio-sacral."

questions.title: Acetylcholine acts on muscarinic and nicotinic receptors
questions.question: The correct statement about acetylcholine:

options.A: Its released from nerve terminals is stimulated by botulinum toxin
options.B: Is synthesized from an amino acid precursor
options.C: It acts on both muscarinic and nicotinic receptors
options.D: Has a half-life of 8 to10 hours in plasma

explanations.A: Incorrect. Botulinum toxin blocks, rather than stimulates, acetylcholine release from nerve terminals -- it cleaves the SNARE proteins vesicles need to fuse with the presynaptic membrane, producing flaccid paralysis, the opposite of stimulation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Acetylcholine is synthesised from choline and acetyl-CoA by choline acetyltransferase, not from an amino acid precursor.
explanations.C: Correct. Acetylcholine acts on both muscarinic receptors (G-protein coupled, at postganglionic parasympathetic effector junctions) and nicotinic receptors (ligand-gated ion channels, at every autonomic ganglion and the skeletal neuromuscular junction). No other autonomic transmitter has this dual receptor-family activation. This is exactly what sets acetylcholine apart from noradrenaline, which activates only adrenergic receptors.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Acetylcholine's half-life in the synapse is a matter of milliseconds, not hours -- it is hydrolysed almost instantly by acetylcholinesterase, which is exactly why acetylcholine itself is unsuitable as a clinical drug.

questions.learning_objective: State that acetylcholine acts on both muscarinic and nicotinic receptors.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: It acts on both muscarinic and nicotinic receptors"

questions.title: Neurotransmitters released from presynaptic terminals
questions.question: Which of the following is correct regarding neurotransmitters and neurotransmission?

options.A: Neurotransmitter release is triggered by the arrival of action potentials in the postsynaptic cell.
options.B: Neurotransmitters are released from the presynaptic nerve terminals.
options.C: Serotonin and dopamine are the primary neurotransmitters in the ANS.
options.D: Intracellular calcium levels drop in the neuron before the neurotransmitter is released.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Release is triggered by an action potential arriving at the presynaptic terminal, not the postsynaptic cell -- the postsynaptic cell is where the released transmitter then acts, not where release originates.
explanations.B: Correct. Neurotransmitters, including acetylcholine, are synthesised and stored in the presynaptic nerve terminal. They are released from that presynaptic terminal into the synaptic cleft when an arriving action potential triggers calcium influx. The postsynaptic cell is where the transmitter then acts, not where it is released from.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Acetylcholine and noradrenaline, not serotonin and dopamine, are the primary neurotransmitters of the autonomic nervous system.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Intracellular calcium rises, not falls, in the presynaptic terminal before release -- calcium influx through voltage-gated channels is the proximate trigger for vesicle fusion and transmitter release.

questions.learning_objective: State that neurotransmitters are released from the presynaptic nerve terminal.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Neurotransmitters are released from the presynaptic nerve terminals."

questions.title: M3 receptor blockade decreases DAG in salivary gland
questions.question: Which of the following is an expected effect of a therapeutic dose of a drug that blocks muscarinic-3 receptors?

options.A: Increased IP3 in intestinal smooth muscle
options.B: Increased sodium influx into the skeletal muscle end plate
options.D: Decreased DAG in salivary gland tissue

explanations.A: Incorrect. A muscarinic-3 blocker would decrease, not increase, IP3 in intestinal smooth muscle -- IP3 generation there depends on M3 receptor stimulation, which the antagonist prevents.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Sodium influx into the skeletal muscle end plate is a nicotinic (not muscarinic) neuromuscular junction event; an M3 blocker at glandular/smooth-muscle muscarinic receptors would not affect it.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cardiac cAMP is governed by the Gi-coupled M2 receptor, not M3 -- a selective M3 blocker would not be expected to change cardiac cAMP.
explanations.D: Correct. M3 muscarinic receptors are Gq-coupled, signalling through phospholipase C to generate IP3 and DAG. Blocking M3 receptors in salivary gland tissue therefore decreases this Gq/IP3-DAG signalling. Because DAG normally drives the secretory response, blocking the receptor that generates it reduces salivary secretion, which is exactly the expected effect of a therapeutic antimuscarinic dose.

questions.subtopic: Muscarinic receptor subtypes and signal transduction
questions.learning_objective: Predict that blocking M3 muscarinic receptors decreases IP3/DAG-mediated glandular secretion.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Decreased DAG in salivary gland tissue"

questions.title: Calcium influx triggers ACh release
questions.question: Influx of what ion causes ACh release into the synaptic cleft, prior to ACh being terminated by acetylcholinesterase (AChE)?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Chloride influx hyperpolarises a cell and is not the trigger for vesicular acetylcholine release at the presynaptic terminal.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Sodium influx underlies the action potential's depolarisation phase as it travels along the axon, but it is calcium influx at the terminal itself that directly triggers vesicle fusion and transmitter release.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Potassium efflux, not influx, repolarises the membrane after an action potential -- it is not the trigger for transmitter release.
explanations.D: Correct. The arrival of an action potential at the presynaptic terminal opens voltage-gated calcium channels. The resulting Ca2+ influx is the proximate trigger causing acetylcholine-containing vesicles to fuse with the presynaptic membrane. This releases their contents into the synaptic cleft, where acetylcholinesterase then terminates acetylcholine's action.

questions.learning_objective: State that calcium influx triggers presynaptic acetylcholine release.

questions.title: Parasympathetic role: accommodation, GI motility, urination
questions.question: Which of the following statements concerning the parasympathetic nervous system is correct?

options.A: The parasympathetic system often discharges as a single, functional system.
options.B: The postganglionic fibers of the parasympathetic division are long compared to those of the sympathetic nervous system.
options.C: The parasympathetic system uses norepinephrine as a neurotransmitter.
options.D: The parasympathetic division is involved in accommodation of near vision, movement of food, and urination.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Unlike the sympathetic system, which tends to discharge diffusely as a single unit ('fight-or-flight'), the parasympathetic system typically activates discretely, organ by organ, rather than as one unified discharge.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Parasympathetic postganglionic fibres are short (the ganglion lies near or within the target organ), while it is the preganglionic fibres that are relatively long -- the reverse of what this option states.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The parasympathetic system uses acetylcholine, not norepinephrine, as its transmitter throughout.
explanations.D: Correct. The parasympathetic ('rest-and-digest') division governs near-vision accommodation via ciliary muscle contraction. It also governs GI motility and secretion, moving food through the gut. It equally governs bladder emptying (urination) via detrusor contraction, the opposite of the sympathetic system's storage-favouring role.

questions.learning_objective: State that the parasympathetic division governs near-vision accommodation, GI motility and urination.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: The parasympathetic division is involved in accommodation of near vision, movement of food, and urination."

questions.title: M3 activation in bronchiolar smooth muscle increases IP3/DAG
questions.question: The activation of muscarinic receptors in bronchiolar smooth muscle is associated with

options.A: decrease in cAMP formation mediated by G-proteins

explanations.A: Incorrect. A decrease in cAMP is the M2 receptor's Gi-coupled signalling pattern in the heart, not the M3 receptor's Gq-coupled pattern in bronchiolar smooth muscle.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Muscarinic activation of bronchiolar smooth muscle activates, rather than inhibits, protein kinase C downstream of the DAG generated by Gq/phospholipase C signalling.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Opening of Na+/K+ cation channels describes fast nicotinic (ligand-gated ion channel) signalling, not the Gq-coupled M3 muscarinic pathway in smooth muscle.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Activation of adenylyl cyclase would raise, not the pathway involved here -- that is the Gs-coupled pattern of a different receptor family, not the Gq-coupled M3 muscarinic receptor.
explanations.E: Correct. M3 muscarinic receptors on bronchiolar smooth muscle are Gq-coupled. Their activation stimulates phospholipase C, generating IP3 and DAG. These second messengers raise intracellular calcium and drive smooth-muscle contraction, producing bronchoconstriction rather than bronchodilation.

questions.subtopic: Muscarinic receptor subtypes and signal transduction
questions.learning_objective: State that muscarinic (M3) activation of bronchiolar smooth muscle increases IP3 and DAG.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: increase in IP3 and DAG"
